items.title: Bernstein逆勢看多AI！上調伺服器、AI晶片出貨預測、稱2026年是ASIC轉折年
paras: Bernstein最新報告指出，儘管AI供應鏈股7月大幅回檔，但四大雲端業者持續上修資本支出，帶動AI伺服器與AI晶片需求增強，因此調高2025至2028年出貨預測，預估全球伺服器市場2028年突破1兆美元，特殊應用晶片（ASIC）、高頻寬記憶體（HBM）、輝達(NVDA-US) Rubin與Google(GOOGL-US) TPU將成未來成長主軸。
儘管七月以來 AI 供應鏈類股在美股市場出現明顯回檔，投資機構 Bernstein 卻在最新公布的最新報告中，逆勢調升了伺服器與 AI 晶片的出貨量預測。
Bernstein 在這份題為《2Q26 AI Server Pulse: Summertime Cool-Down》的報告中指出，近期股價修正主要受三項因素牽動，包括：

市場傳出輝達新一代 Kyber 機架恐面臨延遲；
投資人憂心整體 AI 算力建置是否已經過度擴張；
以及過去幾個月大舉湧入相關類股的動能資金開始全面去槓桿。


分析師將這波修正形容為產業景氣循環中的「夏日降溫」，暗示這只是短期情緒性回檔，而非基本面轉弱的訊號。

四大雲端廠資本支出持續加碼

支撐 Bernstein 樂觀出貨預測的核心邏輯，來自於雲端業者資本支出計畫的持續上修。
報告指出，在今年第二季財報公布後，市場對亞馬遜(AMZN-US) 、微軟(MSFT-US) 、Google 與Meta(META-US) 四大美國雲端巨頭 2026 年資本支出的共識預估，較三月時再上調約15%，並預期 2025 年至 2027 年間將以58%的年複合成長率擴張，總規模逼近 9400 億美元。
若再納入甲骨文(ORCL-US) 以及 CoreWeave(CRWV-US) 、Nebius(YNDX-US) 等新興雲端業者，2027 年的合計資本支出上看 1.11 兆美元。
同一份報告也顯示，全球在建及規劃中的資料中心投資總額，已從四月的約 9600 億美元，一路攀升至約 1.18 萬億美元，反映業者對長期算力需求的信心並未因短線股價波動而動搖。

伺服器市場 2028 年上看破兆美元

在此基礎上，Bernstein 將全球伺服器總出貨量的 2025 至 2028 年複合成長率預測上修至15%，其中搭載高階 GPU 的 AI 伺服器出貨成長率更上調至22%。
若模型成立，全球伺服器市場規模將在 2026 年突破 5600 億美元，並於 2028 年跨越 1 兆美元大關。
以八顆 GPU 為換算基準的高階 AI 伺服器，2026 年出貨量預估將年增48%，2027 年增幅放緩至約13%-17%之間的中段水準，2028 年則因輝達下一代 Rubin Ultra 採用雙晶粒設計，出貨量成長率預期收斂至高個位數。
報告特別提到，隨著「AI代理」應用興起，推論工作已從單次問答演變為連續多步驟流程，帶動以 CPU 為核心的協調運算需求，也讓一般型伺服器出貨到 2028 年仍能維持中段兩位數的年複合成長。

機架化成主流，Kyber 良率仍是變數

隨著 AI 伺服器出貨型態從單一板卡快速轉向整機架化，Bernstein 預估輝達整機櫃出貨量將由 2026 年的約 6.1 萬座，成長到 2027 年的約 8.8 萬座。
報告指出，今年機架形態出貨將正式成為市場主流，傳統 HGX／MGX 板卡形式預估僅消耗整體約35%的 GPU 用量；綜合計算，今年下游實際部署的輝達晶片總量約達 670 萬顆。
產品時程方面，GB300 機架已於去年第四季開始放量出貨，輝達新一代 Vera Rubin 機架及超微半導體(AMD-US) Helios 機架則同步鎖定今年第四季量產，Helios 的客戶名單並涵蓋 Meta、微軟、甲骨文、OpenAI 與 Anthropic。
不過報告也點出潛在風險。再往後一代的 Kyber 機架，其連接運算刀鋒模組的 PCB 背板技術仍是關鍵瓶頸，輝達預料還需與主要 PCB 供應商再花上一到兩季時間磨合設計與良率，才能順利量產。

客製化晶片加速崛起，2026 年成 ASIC 轉折點

除了 GPU 伺服器，Bernstein 也將今年視為ASIC產業發展的重要轉折點。
雲端業者正從小規模試點轉向大規模部署自研晶片，藉此壓低單位算力成本、控管整體擁有成本，並降低對外部 GPU 供應鏈的依賴。
報告預估，ASIC 今年在採用 CoWoS 先進封裝的 AI 晶片總出貨量中占比將達約45%，其中 Google TPU 出貨量預期年增逾90%，在 CoWoS 基礎的 ASIC 出貨中占比約42%。
若以價值計算，ASIC 在整體 XPU（GPU 加 ASIC）市場的占比，將從去年的10%攀升至 2027 年的20%，儘管輝達在訓練端的領先地位依舊穩固。
整體 XPU 市場規模（含 HBM ）預估將從去年約 1900 億美元，在 2027 年擴大至約 5000 億美元；而資料中心 ASIC 市場單獨規模到 2028 年估計落在 1400 億至 1600 億美元之間，當中約有一半來自 HBM 的貢獻。
在競爭態勢上，Google TPU 預估將在 2027 年拿下整體 ASIC 市場近70%份額，2028 年約為60%，單看 TPU 一項，2028 年對應市場規模至少達 900 億美元。
產業鏈訊號也相互呼應：

博通(AVGO-US) 已與 Google 簽下長期合約，將為其開發並供應未來多個世代的 TPU 直到 2031 年，同時擴大與 Meta 的合作關係；
邁威爾科技(MRVL-US) 的客製化加速器則已在四大雲端業者全面放量出貨；
聯發科(2454-TW) 同時拿下 Google 兩項 TPU 專案（分別為 v8t 與 v9 世代），並已將今年 ASIC 營收展望上修至「超過 20 億美元」，同時看好 2027 年 ASIC 可及市場規模達 800 億美元，目標市占率15%-20%。


晶片規格方面，Google Ironwood（即 TPU v7）相較上一代在每瓦效能提升一倍、HBM 容量擴增六倍，單一機架可整合 256 顆加速器；亞馬遜 Trainium 3 的 FP8 運算效能約為前代 Trainium 2 的兩倍，下一代 Trainium 4 單顆晶片的 BF16 算力預估將逼近 3900 TFLOPS。

供應鏈數據交叉驗證，估值與獲利出現背離

Bernstein 也透過供應鏈端的營收表現，交叉驗證上述出貨預測的合理性。
深度參與亞馬遜、Meta ASIC 專案的緯穎與智邦，市場共識預估今年營收將分別年增36% 和 54%；去年因美系 IDM 專案結束而營收重挫四成一的世芯(3661-TW) ，今年則在 Trainium 3 專案帶動下，市場預期營收有望翻倍成長，台灣 ASIC 相關公司的月營收成長也在今年六月重新加速。
此外，台灣對美出口中涵蓋 AI 伺服器的資通與視聽產品，第二季季增63%，主要動能來自 GB300、ASIC 與一般型伺服器同步放量；儘管 ODM／OEM 廠商的庫存金額自 2024 年以來持續攀升，但庫存天數仍處於歷史正常區間。
不過報告也提醒，目前市場正出現「估值收縮、獲利預測卻同步上修」的矛盾現象。年初至今追蹤的 29 檔 AI 供應鏈個股中，多達 21 檔本益比遭到壓縮，僅 7 檔估值擴張，但同期多數公司 2026、2027 年每股盈餘的市場共識預估卻持續上修，反映投資人對資本支出可持續性與投資報酬率仍存在明顯分歧。
另一項不確定因素則是 HBM 記憶體的定價。2027 年 HBM 漲價已幾成定局，僅漲幅仍待議定；由於博通等 ASIC 廠商多半代客戶採購 HBM 並將其計入自身 ASIC 營收，HBM 漲幅越高，客戶轉向直接採購以規避加價的誘因也將隨之增加，進而牽動整體 ASIC 市場規模的估算。
Bernstein 在報告最後列出未來十二個月值得留意的觀察指標，包括

輝達 Rubin 機架的實際出貨進度；
Rubin Ultra 與 Google TPU v8 的推進節奏；
亞馬遜 Trainium 3 的落地情形；
代理式 AI 對 CPU 需求的實際拉動力道；
以及 T-glass、ABF 載板供給狀況，還有電力機架與共同封裝光學（CPO）技術的放量時程。

items.title: 高盛警告超大型科技股壟斷格局瓦解 市場集中度拐點已現
items.title_en: Goldman Warns of Tech Monopoly Collapse, Market Concentration Turning Point Arrives
paras: 長期以來，全球市場深受少數超大型科技股 (Hyperscalers) 主導，但根據最新研究報告，這一持續逾 15 年的市場集中格局可能正迎來結構性拐點，權力平衡正在發生劇烈震盪。
高盛與阿波羅 (Apollo) 等機構的分析師指出，隨著 AI 資本開支壓力增加及總體經濟環境改變，投資者應準備迎接一個更為多元、由盈利驅動的「大擴散」時代。

科技巨頭優勢喪失

高盛首席全球股票策略師 Peter Oppenheimer 指出，儘管科技領域目前似乎並未出現傳統的「估值泡沫」，但可能正陷入「盈利泡沫」中。自 ChatGPT 爆發以來，科技巨頭為維持 AI 領先地位，展開了激進的資本開支競賽。這種龐大的支出正從根本上改變科技股的財務結構，持續侵蝕其一度引以為傲的自由現金流。
數據顯示，這類超大型企業在現金流收益率上的優勢，相較於其他價值型市場 (如歐洲) 已大幅縮小。這導致科技股曾經擁有的高溢價幾乎消失，迫使市場進入「健康的正常化」進程。

等權重指數的崛起

壟斷格局瓦解的最直觀證據在於市場參與度的擴散。自 2009 年以來，等權重 (Equal-weighted) 標普 500 指數首次以超過 7.3% 的幅度勝過市值加權 (Market-cap-weighted) 指數。這反映出美股不再僅靠幾家「大權值股」支撐，資金正流向被低估的傳統工業、日本、歐洲及新興市場。
阿波羅首席經濟學家 Torsten Slok 更進一步警告，傳統的 60/40 投資組合 (60% 股票、40% 債券) 已經失效。他指出，隨著 AI 交易熱潮放緩，在高通膨、政府債務攀升至 GDP 175% 的背景下，過去 40 年的投資邏輯正面臨考驗。

未來展望：回歸基本面與多元化配置

這場市場轉向並非僅由情緒驅動，而是建立在紮實的盈利增長之上。
隨著資本成本上升 (Higher for longer)，盈利增長而非單純的估值擴張，已成為股市回報的核心驅動力。AI 大規模資本支出的溢出效應，正帶動長期被忽視的能源、國防及關鍵基礎建設等傳統行業重估。
高盛認為，隨著個股相關性下降與領漲類股的切換，跨地域、跨行業的均衡配置將是獲取真實回報的關鍵。投資者需從過去十年的極度集中，轉向更全面的資產佈局，以因應投資環境的結構性變革。
paras_en: For over 15 years, the global market has been dominated by a few large tech stocks, known as hyperscalers. However, according to a recent research report, this prolonged market concentration may be facing a structural turning point, with power dynamics experiencing a dramatic shift.

Analysts from Goldman Sachs and Apollo, among others, suggest that as AI capital expenditure pressure increases and the overall economic environment changes, investors should prepare for a more diversified, profit-driven "great dispersal" era.
Tech giants losing their edge

Goldman Sachs' Chief Global Equity Strategist Peter Oppenheimer notes that, although the tech sector may not appear to be in a traditional "valuation bubble," it may be experiencing a "profit bubble." Since the ChatGPT explosion, tech giants have launched aggressive capital expenditure competitions to maintain their AI leadership position. This massive spending is fundamentally changing the financial structure of tech stocks, continuously eroding their once-vaunted free cash flow.

Data shows that these large enterprises have significantly narrowed their cash flow yield advantage compared to other value-oriented markets (such as Europe). This has led to the near disappearance of the high premium previously enjoyed by tech stocks, forcing the market to enter a "healthy normalization" process.
The rise of equal-weight indices

The most direct evidence of the monopoly collapse is the dispersion of market participation. Since 2009, the equal-weighted S&P 500 index has surpassed the market-cap-weighted index by over 7.3% for the first time. This reflects that the US stock market is no longer solely supported by a few "large-weight stocks," with capital flowing towards undervalued traditional industries, Japan, Europe, and emerging markets.

Apollo's Chief Economist Torsten Slok further warns that traditional 60/40 investment portfolios (60% stocks, 40% bonds) have become ineffective. He notes that, with the AI trading frenzy subsiding, in the context of high inflation and government debt rising to 175% of GDP, the investment logic of the past 40 years is being put to the test.
Future outlook: returning to fundamentals and diversified allocation
This market shift is not driven by emotions alone, but is built on solid profit growth.

As capital costs rise (higher for longer), profit growth, rather than simple valuation expansion, has become the core driver of stock market returns. The spillover effect of AI massive capital expenditure is driving long-neglected traditional industries such as energy, defense, and critical infrastructure to be revalued.

Goldman believes that, as individual stock correlations decrease and sector rotation occurs, cross-regional and cross-industry balanced allocation will be key to achieving real returns. Investors need to transition from the extreme concentration of the past decade to a more comprehensive asset allocation to adapt to the structural changes in the investment environment.

items.title: 美股獨霸時代鬆動！高盛：分散投資重新當道  資金轉向日本、亞太與新興市場
items.title_en: US Stock Dominance Erodes as Goldman Sachs Sees Shift to Diversified Investing
paras: 長達十五年之久的美股獨大格局，如今出現鬆動跡象。高盛首席全球股票策略師Peter Oppenheimer在最新發布的策略報告中直言，全球股市正邁入一場「健康的正常化」過程，資金版圖不再獨厚單一市場或單一產業，分散配置的價值正逐漸浮現。
Oppenheimer觀察到，自2025年初起，這股「大擴散」趨勢明顯加快腳步。過去被視為全球股市火車頭的美國，反而在主要市場中敬陪末座；相對地，日本、亞太與新興市場以當地貨幣計算的漲幅則居於前列。
造成此番板塊挪移的關鍵，在於科技巨頭近年瘋狂擴張的資本支出，正逐步吃掉自身的自由現金流收益率，迫使市場重新檢視科技股的估值溢價。
與此同時，這波資本支出熱潮所帶來的外溢效應，反而讓工業等傳統產業重獲市場青睞，成長前景與估值評價雙雙獲得提振。
Oppenheimer在報告中特別點出一項關鍵，即這次的板塊輪動並非由估值膨脹或降息預期所推動，而是實實在在的獲利表現撐起的行情。
他認為，市值與獲利雙雙高度集中於少數股票的現象持續逾十年後，如今正迎來結構性的轉捩點，投資人透過真正的多元配置獲取超額報酬的機會，正悄悄增加。

科技股風光不再？資本支出反噬現金流優勢

回顧金融海嘯後的十多年，科技業憑藉輕資產經營模式、雲端與軟體需求的爆炸性成長，加上零利率環境撐起的估值溢價，一路推升獲利率與股東權益報酬率，穩坐全球資金最愛的寶座。
然而，ChatGPT問世後點燃的AI軍備競賽，徹底改變了遊戲規則。
Oppenheimer指出，超大型科技公司為了搶占AI版圖，展開一場前所未見的資本支出競賽，這場「超級週期」正從根本上侵蝕科技業原本引以為傲的財務體質，龐大投資持續吃掉自由現金流，逼得這些企業不得不轉向債市與股市籌措資金。
若以自由現金流收益率衡量，向來由科技巨頭撐腰的美股，相對於歐洲等價值型市場的優勢已明顯收斂，這正是近期市場相對表現出現輪動的基本面依據。
再加上政府債務攀升、通膨壓力揮之不去，以及公債供給增加，資金成本水漲船高，使得獲利成長重新成為股市報酬的主要引擎。

傳統產業迎來重估，獲利才是硬道理

值得留意的是，這波市場擴散並非空中樓閣，而是建立在扎實的獲利基礎之上。
Oppenheimer強調，不只獲利表現本身亮眼，分析師對獲利預期的修正方向也持續向上調整，等於為股市的基本面提供了雙重驗證。
超大型科技公司與晶片廠商的鉅額資本支出，加上各國政府為了能源安全、關鍵基礎設施及國防建設而加碼的財政支出，共同催生出這一輪資本支出超級週期。
而其外溢效應，也讓長期被市場冷落的工業等傳統類股重新獲得關注，成長前景與估值同步獲得提振。
從國家層面來看，各地區的股東權益報酬率整體仍維持高檔，個股之間的相關性下降，隨著領漲類股不斷輪替，選股創造超額報酬的空間正在擴大。
Oppenheimer指出，雖然美股整體本益比因科技股拖累而下滑，但若從股東權益報酬率角度審視，美國市場仍是全球最具吸引力的地方。

集中度拐點浮現，分散配置重新當道

高盛認為，個股相關性下滑，加上近期動能策略迅速瓦解，正加速市場領導權的洗牌，也為投資人在成長型股票中精選標的、創造價值提供了更有利的環境。
Oppenheimer的核心論點是，在市值與獲利雙重面向上經歷逾十年的極端集中之後，全球股市正經歷一場健康的正常化修正，多元化配置終於重新獲得實質報酬。他預期，這股趨勢仍將持續演進。
分析指出，對投資人而言，這代表過去「全押美股科技巨頭」的策略，性價比正在下滑；取而代之的，是跨地域、跨產業的均衡配置邏輯，正重新站上舞台中央。
paras_en: The long-standing dominance of US stocks is showing signs of erosion, according to Goldman Sachs' chief global stock strategist Peter Oppenheimer. In a recent strategy report, Oppenheimer stated that the global stock market is entering a 'healthy normalization' process, where capital is no longer concentrated in a single market or industry, and diversified investing is gaining traction.

Oppenheimer noted that since the beginning of 2025, the trend of 'big dispersion' has accelerated. Historically, the US was seen as the locomotive of the global stock market, but it is now lagging behind in major markets. In contrast, Japan, Asia, and emerging markets are leading the pack in terms of local currency gains.

The key driver behind this shift is the massive capital expenditure by tech giants in recent years, which is gradually eating into their free cash flow yields, forcing the market to reevaluate the valuation of tech stocks.

Meanwhile, the spillover effect of this capital expenditure wave has boosted the appeal of traditional industries such as manufacturing, which are regaining market attention, with growth prospects and valuations both receiving a boost.
Oppenheimer highlighted that this shift is not driven by valuation expansion or interest rate expectations, but rather by the underlying profit performance.

He believes that the phenomenon of high concentration of market value and profits in a few stocks has persisted for over a decade and is now reaching a structural turning point, presenting opportunities for investors to achieve excess returns through genuine diversification.
The glory days of tech stocks are over? Capital expenditure is biting into cash flow superiority

Looking back over the past decade and a half, the tech industry has benefited from its lean asset management model, explosive growth in cloud and software demand, and valuation premiums supported by zero-interest-rate environments, propelling profit rates and shareholder returns to the top of the global capital flow hierarchy.
However, the emergence of AI-powered ChatGPT has ignited a new era of AI arms racing, fundamentally changing the game.

Oppenheimer pointed out that the super-large tech companies are engaging in an unprecedented capital expenditure competition to capture the AI landscape, which is eroding the financial health of these companies from the ground up, forcing them to turn to debt markets and equity markets to raise funds.

If measured by free cash flow yields, the US stock market, which has long been supported by tech giants, is now converging with European value-oriented markets, providing a fundamental basis for the recent market rotation.

Additionally, rising government debt, persistent inflation pressures, and increased government bond supply are driving up capital costs, making profit growth the primary engine of stock market returns.
Traditional industries regain favor, profit is the hard truth
It's worth noting that this market dispersion is not a pie-in-the-sky phenomenon, but rather one built on a solid foundation of profit performance.

Oppenheimer emphasized that not only is profit performance impressive, but analysts' upward revisions to profit expectations are also ongoing, providing a double validation of the market's fundamental underpinnings.

The massive capital expenditure by super-large tech companies and chip manufacturers, combined with governments' increased fiscal spending for energy security, critical infrastructure, and national defense, has given birth to this super-cycle of capital expenditure.
The spillover effect has also revived the interest in long-neglected industrial stocks, with growth prospects and valuations both receiving a boost.

From a country perspective, the overall shareholder return rates remain high, and individual stock correlations are declining, as leading stocks continue to rotate, creating space for investors to generate excess returns through stock selection.

Oppenheimer noted that although the US market's overall P/E ratio has declined due to the drag from tech stocks, from a shareholder return rate perspective, the US market remains the most attractive destination globally.
Concentration threshold appears, diversified investing re-emerges

Goldman Sachs believes that declining stock correlations and the recent collapse of momentum strategies are accelerating the rotation of market leadership, creating a more favorable environment for investors to select growth stocks and create value.

Oppenheimer's core argument is that, after experiencing over a decade of extreme concentration in both market value and profit, the global stock market is undergoing a healthy normalization correction, and diversified investing is finally regaining its practical returns. He expects this trend to continue.

For investors, this means that the strategy of 'all-in' on US tech giants is becoming less attractive in terms of value for money; in its place, a balanced configuration logic that spans regions and industries is regaining center stage.

items.title: 誰是AI競賽大贏家？黃仁勳點名馬斯克坐擁三大護城河
items.title_en: Who is the AI Competition Winner? Huang Renxun Points to Musk's Three-Pronged Moat
paras: 輝達(NVDA-US) 執行長黃仁勳最新一段訪談影片近日在社群媒體引發熱議。他在談及未來AI產業競爭時，點名特斯拉(TSLA-US) 與SpaceX(SPCX-US) 執行長馬斯克，認為馬斯克在AI競賽中處於「絕佳位置」（phenomenal position），其優勢並非來自個人風格，而是建立在算力基礎設施、真實世界數據，以及多項AI應用布局之上。
黃仁勳指出，馬斯克最大的優勢，在於擁有其他競爭者難以短時間複製的基礎設施與數據資源。特斯拉持續累積全球車隊產生的大量駕駛數據，同時部署大量輝達硬體支撐AI運算，再加上xAI、特斯拉自動駕駛與Optimus人形機器人三大業務同步推進，使馬斯克在AI時代占據重要戰略位置。
真實世界數據成AI競爭關鍵
根據流傳的影片內容，黃仁勳在談到AI產業未來發展時表示，採集真實世界數據的成本非常高，而馬斯克擁有巨大的優勢。這項優勢主要來自兩大面向，包括AI算力基礎設施與真實世界數據。
首先，在算力方面，黃仁勳指出，特斯拉用於自動駕駛訓練的AI工廠擁有大量輝達GPU，是全球強大的AI訓練平台之一，能為FSD（Full Self-Driving）模型持續迭代提供充足算力。
其次，在數據方面，特斯拉擁有全球規模最大的連網汽車車隊之一，每天持續收集駕駛環境、道路狀況以及車輛運行數據。相較於依賴公開數據訓練模型的AI公司，特斯拉能夠持續取得來自真實世界的新數據，而這類數據取得成本極高，也是自動駕駛模型持續進化的重要基礎。
黃仁勳認為，馬斯克在AI時代具備天然優勢，而這種優勢是經過多年累積形成，並非短時間內可以複製。
AI三大戰場：xAI、自動駕駛與人形機器人
除了算力與數據優勢外，黃仁勳也強調，馬斯克正在布局AI產業最重要的三大方向，包括基礎模型、自動駕駛以及人形機器人。
其中，xAI負責基礎認知智能，也就是基礎模型與一般AI能力；特斯拉則聚焦自動駕駛；Optimus則負責人形機器人發展。黃仁勳表示，這三個方向正是AI未來最重要的三大戰場。
這也代表，未來AI競爭將不只是發生在聊天機器人或大型語言模型之間，而會進一步延伸至機器人與物理世界應用。若將基礎模型視為負責「思考」，自動駕駛負責「理解現實世界」，人形機器人則負責「進入現實世界並執行任務」，三者共同構成下一階段AI產業發展的重要閉環。
AI競爭從模型轉向基礎設施
近年AI產業競爭焦點逐漸從模型參數規模，轉向更難複製的基礎設施能力。一方面，大模型推動GPU與資料中心投資快速成長；另一方面，科技公司也開始意識到，高品質真實世界數據正成為新的稀缺資源。
在此趨勢下，自動駕駛成為AI產業的重要數據來源。特斯拉數百萬輛連網汽車每天持續產生駕駛數據，不僅用於FSD訓練，也讓公司建立其他AI企業難以複製的數據護城河。
同時，馬斯克持續推進AI版圖擴張，xAI負責訓練新一代基礎模型，特斯拉推進FSD與Robotaxi，Optimus則被定位為未來可大規模部署的人形機器人平台。
黃仁勳將這三項業務並列為AI未來重要發展方向，也意味著他認為AI競爭將更多圍繞算力、數據與機器人應用展開，而不只是誰擁有性能最強的大模型。
黃仁勳再凸顯輝達AI核心地位
值得注意的是，黃仁勳在分析馬斯克優勢時，也再次強調AI基礎設施的重要性。無論是訓練基礎模型，或是推動自動駕駛與機器人系統，都需要持續投入大規模GPU叢集與資料中心，而輝達GPU仍是目前AI訓練與推理基礎設施的重要組成部分。
黃仁勳過去多次提出，未來每一家大型企業都將建造自己的「AI工廠」，AI時代的核心競爭力不只在演算法，而在於能否透過算力基礎設施，持續將數據轉化為智慧。
此次以特斯拉為例，黃仁勳再次強調，真正難以複製的並非單一模型，而是長期累積形成的算力、真實世界數據與應用場景相互強化的飛輪效應。
paras_en: NVIDIA (NVDA-US) CEO Huang Renxun's latest interview video has sparked heated discussion on social media. He pointed out that Tesla (TSLA-US) and SpaceX (SPCX-US) CEO Musk is in a 'phenomenal position' in AI competition, and his advantage is not just due to personal style, but rather built on computing infrastructure, real-world data, and multiple AI application layouts.

Huang Renxun pointed out that Musk's biggest advantage is that he has a foundation and data resources that are difficult for other competitors to replicate in a short period of time. Tesla continues to accumulate a large amount of driving data from its global vehicle fleet, while deploying a large number of NVIDIA hardware to support AI computing, and pushing forward three major businesses: xAI, Tesla Autopilot, and Optimus humanoid robots, making Musk occupy an important strategic position in the AI era.
Real-world data is a key factor in AI competition

According to the leaked video content, Huang Renxun said that collecting real-world data is very expensive, and Musk has a huge advantage. This advantage mainly comes from two aspects: AI computing infrastructure and real-world data.

Firstly, in terms of computing power, Huang Renxun pointed out that Tesla's AI factory for autonomous driving training has a large number of NVIDIA GPUs, which is one of the world's strongest AI training platforms, providing sufficient computing power for the FSD (Full Self-Driving) model to continue iterating.

Secondly, in terms of data, Tesla has one of the largest connected vehicle fleets in the world, continuously collecting driving environment, road conditions, and vehicle operation data every day. Compared to AI companies that rely on public data to train models, Tesla can continuously obtain new data from the real world, and this type of data is extremely expensive to obtain, and is an important foundation for the continuous evolution of autonomous driving models.
Huang Renxun believes that Musk has a natural advantage in the AI era, and this advantage has been formed over many years and cannot be replicated in a short period of time.
AI's three major battlefields: xAI, autonomous driving, and humanoid robots

In addition to computing power and data advantages, Huang Renxun also emphasized that Musk is laying out the three most important directions in the AI industry: foundation models, autonomous driving, and humanoid robots.

Among them, xAI is responsible for basic cognitive intelligence, also known as foundation models and general AI capabilities; Tesla focuses on autonomous driving; and Optimus is responsible for humanoid robot development. Huang Renxun said that these three directions are the most important three battlefields in AI's future.

This also means that future AI competition will not only occur between chatbots or large language models, but will also extend to robots and physical world applications. If we consider foundation models as responsible for 'thinking', autonomous driving as responsible for 'understanding the real world', and humanoid robots as responsible for 'entering the real world and executing tasks', the three together form an important closed loop in the next stage of AI industry development.
AI competition shifts from model parameters to infrastructure

In recent years, AI industry competition has shifted from model parameter size to more difficult-to-replicate infrastructure capabilities. On the one hand, large models have driven rapid growth in GPU and data center investments; on the other hand, technology companies have begun to realize that high-quality real-world data has become a new scarce resource.

In this trend, autonomous driving has become an important data source for the AI industry. Tesla's hundreds of millions of connected vehicles produce driving data every day, not only for FSD training, but also for building a data moat that other AI companies cannot replicate.

At the same time, Musk continues to push forward the expansion of the AI landscape, with xAI responsible for training the next generation of foundation models, Tesla pushing forward FSD and Robotaxi, and Optimus positioned as a future large-scale deployable humanoid robot platform.

Huang Renxun lists these three businesses as important development directions for AI's future, which means he believes that AI competition will focus more on computing power, data, and robot applications, rather than who has the most powerful large model.
Huang Renxun again highlights NVIDIA's core position in AI

It's worth noting that Huang Renxun, in analyzing Musk's advantages, also again emphasizes the importance of AI infrastructure. Whether training foundation models or pushing forward autonomous driving and robot systems, it requires continuous investment in large-scale GPU clusters and data centers, and NVIDIA GPUs are still an important component of AI training and reasoning infrastructure.

Huang Renxun has previously pointed out that in the future, every large company will build its own 'AI factory', and the core competitive advantage in the AI era is not just in algorithms, but in being able to transform data into intelligence through computing power infrastructure.

This time, using Tesla as an example, Huang Renxun again emphasizes that what is difficult to replicate is not a single model, but the long-term accumulation of computing power, real-world data, and application scenarios that reinforce each other in a flywheel effect.

items.title: Samsung SDI全力衝刺全固態電池產能 2028年後產能恐供不應求
items.title_en: Samsung SDI Accelerates Full‑Solid‑State Battery Capacity; Post‑2028 Capacity May Outstrip Supply
paras: 2026年08月05日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ 南韓電池廠Samsung SDI持續推進全固態電池布局。公司維持2027年下半年量產人形機器人用全固態電池的目標，已累積的訂單可望支撐生產線運作至2029年；若今年稍晚再取得新訂單，現有產能自2028年起可能出現供不應求。
為因應下一代電池需求，Samsung SDI今年7月宣布，將於2026年至2040年間投資共25兆韓元，擴建南韓蔚山與天安兩大生產基地。其中，蔚山廠將建置全固態電池、儲能系統用磷酸鐵鋰電池及鈉離子電池量產產線；天安廠則定位為技術驗證中心，支援未來量產導入與製程優化。
在技術布局方面，Samsung SDI已完成全固態電池試產線建置，並向電動車、具身智慧及人形機器人等潛在客戶送樣測試，未來將由蔚山新產線承接試產成果，率先於南韓展開商業化，再逐步擴展至海外生產基地。
市場需求正沿著不同應用領域逐步擴大。
固態電池已率先應用於消費電子產品，工業機器人也進入實測階段；無人機、智慧機器人等新興應用則透過半固態電池逐步導入，電動車與人形機器人預期將成為全固態電池下一波主要成長動能。TrendForce集邦預估，全球固態電池需求將於2030年突破206GWh，2035年擴大至740GWh，其中人形機器人將是主要應用領域之一。
隨著半固態電池已率先實現量產，業界普遍視其為邁向全固態電池的重要過渡技術，而全固態電池則預計於2027年至2028年展開首波商業化，並自2028年開始進入GWh級量產應用階段。
市場對Samsung SDI營運展望也轉趨樂觀。Eugene Investment & Securities預估，公司可望於2026年恢復獲利，並首次給予「買進」評等，目標價500,000韓元。分析師認為，隨著訂單能見度延伸至2029年，以及全固態電池量產時程明確，公司中長期成長動能可望逐步浮現。消息激勵Samsung SDI股價上漲2.2%，至428,500韓元。

paras_en: August 5, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center) – South Korean battery maker Samsung SDI continues to push its full‑solid‑state battery (FSSB) strategy. The company maintains its target to begin mass production of FSSBs for humanoid robots in the second half of 2027, and the orders already accumulated are expected to keep the production line running through 2029; if new orders are secured later this year, existing capacity could become insufficient from 2028 onward.

To meet next‑generation battery demand, Samsung SDI announced in July that it will invest a total of 25 trillion won between 2026 and 2040 to expand its two major plants in Ulsan and Cheonan, South Korea. The Ulsan facility will build mass‑production lines for full‑solid‑state batteries, lithium‑iron‑phosphate batteries for energy‑storage systems, and sodium‑ion batteries, while the Cheonan plant will serve as a technology‑validation center to support future mass‑production rollout and process optimisation.

On the technology front, Samsung SDI has completed the construction of a pilot line for full‑solid‑state batteries and has sent sample units to potential customers in electric vehicles, embodied AI, and humanoid robots for testing. The results of the pilot will be taken over by the new Ulsan line, which will first commercialise the technology domestically before gradually expanding to overseas production sites.

Market demand is expanding across different application areas. Solid‑state batteries have already been adopted in consumer electronics, and industrial robots are entering the testing phase. Emerging applications such as drones and smart robots are being introduced via semi‑solid‑state batteries, while electric vehicles and humanoid robots are expected to become the next major growth drivers for full‑solid‑state batteries. TrendForce forecasts global solid‑state battery demand to exceed 206 GWh by 2030 and reach 740 GWh by 2035, with humanoid robots being one of the key application segments.

With semi‑solid‑state batteries now in mass production, the industry generally views them as an important stepping‑stone toward full‑solid‑state technology. Full‑solid‑state batteries are expected to see their first wave of commercialisation in 2027‑2028 and to enter GWh‑scale production from 2028 onward.

Market outlook for Samsung SDI’s operations has become more optimistic. Eugene Investment & Securities projects that the company will return to profitability in 2026 and upgrades its rating to “Buy” with a target price of 500,000 won. Analysts note that order visibility extending to 2029 and a clear timeline for FSSB mass production should gradually reveal the company’s mid‑to‑long‑term growth momentum. The news lifted Samsung SDI’s share price by 2.2% to 428,500 won.

items.title: 日本薪資連六月增長 勞動力市場緊俏強化日銀升息預期
items.title_en: Japan's Wages Rise for Sixth Straight Month, Boosting BOJ Rate Hike Expectations
paras: 日本勞動省周三 (5 日) 公佈的最新數據顯示，受惠於強勁的企業獲利與持續緊俏的勞動力市場，日本薪資增長勢頭穩健，進一步強化了市場對日本銀行在未來幾個月再次升息的預期。
數據顯示，日本 6 月名目薪資年增 3.4%，符合經濟學家預期，這也是名目薪資連續第五個月增幅超過 3%，創下 34 年來最長的紀錄。特別是，調整通膨後的實質薪資成長了 1.6% 至 1.7%，不僅連續第六個月上揚，更寫下 2021 年以來最長的連漲紀錄。
其中，6 月的名目薪資的加速，顯示薪資成長的動力已從波動較大的獎金 (一次性支付) 轉向更具持續性的固定薪資。這種結構性轉變正是日本銀行長期觀察的重點，認為這代表通膨正逐漸由需求驅動，而非單純的成本推升。
薪資的強勁表現主要反映了今年「春鬥」薪資談判的豐碩成果。日本最大工會聯合會 (Rengo) 爭取到超過 5% 的加薪，而大型企業如經團連 (Keidanren) 成員的平均加薪幅度更達到 5.4%。此外，超過 70% 的企業表示，加薪的主要動力是為了在緊俏的勞動力市場中招募與留住人才。
日本銀行總裁植田和男在近期的記者會中展現出鷹派立場，警示價格上行的風險正在加劇。
分析師認為，穩健的薪資增長讓日銀更有底氣維持政策正常化路徑，升息時機最快可能落在 9 月，或者不遲於今年 12 月。此外，日本政府近期與美國協調干預匯市以支撐日元，也強化了市場對於政策提前調整的預期。
儘管薪資漲勢亮眼，但食品價格通膨仍維持在高點，讓一般家庭對生活成本感到憂心。為減緩民眾壓力，日本政府計畫從明年 4 月起暫時調降食品銷售稅，並向低收入戶發放補貼。
大和證券 (Daiwa Securities) 經濟學家 Kento Minami 表示，隨著中東局勢升溫導致企業加速轉嫁成本，實質薪資在今年 11 月後仍可能面臨暫時轉負的下行壓力。
paras_en: Japan's labor ministry reported on Wednesday (5th) that the country's wages rose for the sixth consecutive month, driven by strong corporate profits and a tight labor market, further solidifying market expectations of another rate hike by the Bank of Japan in the coming months.
The data showed that Japan's nominal wages rose 3.4% in June, in line with economists' expectations, marking the fifth consecutive month of wage growth above 3%, a record 34-year high.
Notably, real wages, adjusted for inflation, grew 1.6% to 1.7%, marking the sixth consecutive month of gains and the longest streak since 2021.

The acceleration in nominal wages in June suggests that wage growth is shifting from volatile bonuses to more sustainable fixed salaries, a structural change that the Bank of Japan has been closely watching, as it believes it represents a shift from cost-push to demand-driven inflation.

The strong wage performance mainly reflects the outcome of this year's 'spring offensive' wage negotiations, with Japan's largest labor union, Rengo, securing over 5% wage hikes, while large companies, such as Keidanren members, saw an average wage increase of 5.4%.
More than 70% of companies said that wage hikes were mainly driven by the need to attract and retain talent in a tight labor market.
Bank of Japan Governor Haruhiko Kuroda has taken a hawkish stance in recent press conferences, warning of increasing risks of price hikes.

Analysts believe that stable wage growth will give the BOJ more confidence to stick to its normalization path, with the next rate hike potentially coming as early as September or not later than December.
The Japanese government's recent coordination with the US to intervene in the foreign exchange market to support the yen has also strengthened market expectations of an earlier policy adjustment.
Despite the strong wage growth, food price inflation remains high, causing concern among households about living costs.
To alleviate public pressure, the Japanese government plans to temporarily lower food sales tax from April next year and provide subsidies to low-income households.

Daiwa Securities economist Kento Minami said that with the Middle East situation escalating, leading to companies accelerating cost transfers, real wages may still face downward pressure in November and beyond.

items.title: 印度央行維持利率不變 在通膨壓力與地緣政治迷霧中尋求韌性
items.title_en: India's Central Bank Keeps Rates Unchanged Amid Inflation Pressure and Geopolitical Uncertainty
paras: 印度央行 (RBI) 周三 (5 日) 宣布將基準利率維持在 5.25%，這是央行連續第五次維持利率不變。儘管印度的零售通膨率已突破了 4% 的中期目標，由總裁馬洛特拉 (Sanjay Malhotra) 領導的貨幣政策委員會仍全體一致投票通過維持回購利率，並保持中立的政策立場。
數據顯示，受油價飆升影響，印度 6 月份消費者物價指數 (CPI) 觸及 18 個月高點 4.38%。雖然整體通膨超標，但馬洛特拉強調，核心通膨 (不含食品與能源) 仍維持在 3.7% 的適度水準，且目前尚未看到價格壓力全面擴散的跡象。
央行預計，整體通膨將在第三季達到峰值後回落，並將全年度通膨預測從 5.1% 略微下調至 5.0%。
印度目前仍是全球增長最快的主要經濟體之一，1 月至 3 月季度的 GDP 成長率達 7.8%。然而，未來的經濟前景顯得「模糊」。馬洛特拉指出，西南季風的不確定性、聖嬰現象 (El Niño) 以及中東地區 (特別是伊朗) 的衝突，都為成長帶來挑戰。
由於印度約 85% 至 90% 的燃料需求依賴進口，地緣政治引發的能源價格波動是最大的隱憂。
政策公布後，印度基準 Nifty 50 指數表現持平，10 年期國債殖利率則下滑至約 6.77%。在匯率方面，儘管印度盧比在政策公布後交易價格略有回升，但受資本外流與地緣政治導致的美元走強影響，盧比今年仍是亞洲表現最差的貨幣之一。
雖然央行目前選擇觀望，但匯豐銀行 (HSBC) 等研究機構警告，若通膨從 10 月起連續八個月維持在 5% 以上，央行將難以坐視不管。許多經濟學家預測，隨著 8 月底 GDP 數據的公布，若通膨壓力持續，印度央行可能會在 10 月或 12 月開啟升息循環。
paras_en: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced on Wednesday that it would keep its benchmark interest rate at 5.25%, marking the fifth consecutive time the central bank has left rates unchanged. Despite India's retail inflation rate exceeding the 4% medium-term target, the Monetary Policy Committee, led by Governor Sanjay Malhotra, unanimously voted to maintain the repo rate and retain a neutral policy stance.

Data showed that India's consumer price index (CPI) reached an 18-month high of 4.38% in June, driven by rising oil prices. Although overall inflation exceeded the target, Malhotra emphasized that core inflation (excluding food and energy) remained moderate at 3.7% and that there were no signs of broad-based price pressures.
The central bank expects overall inflation to peak in the third quarter before easing and has slightly lowered its full-year inflation forecast to 5.0% from 5.1%.

India remains one of the fastest-growing major economies, with a GDP growth rate of 7.8% in the January-March quarter. However, the economic outlook is 'uncertain'. Malhotra cited the uncertainty of the southwest monsoon, the El Niño phenomenon, and conflicts in the Middle East (particularly in Iran) as challenges to growth.
As India relies on imports for 85-90% of its fuel needs, geopolitical tensions that lead to energy price volatility are a major concern.

Following the policy announcement, the Nifty 50 index was little changed, while the 10-year government bond yield fell to around 6.77%. The Indian rupee, which had initially risen after the policy announcement, remains one of the worst-performing currencies in Asia this year due to capital outflows and a strong US dollar driven by geopolitical tensions.

Although the central bank has chosen to wait and watch for now, research institutions such as HSBC have warned that if inflation remains above 5% from October for eight consecutive months, the RBI will find it difficult to remain inactive. Many economists predict that if inflationary pressures persist, the RBI may start a rate hike cycle in October or December, following the release of GDP data at the end of August.

items.title: 公開押寶下月升息？美財長：深信日本央行總裁植田和男將「做出最佳決策」
items.title_en: US Treasury Secretary Expresses Confidence in BOJ's Decision-Making Ahead of Potential Rate Hike
paras: 美國財長貝森特周二 (4 日) 接受《NHK》專訪時表示，他認識日本央行總裁植田和男逾 15 年，深信植田會採取對日本經濟最有利的經濟決定。他並直言，日本通膨升溫部分源自弱勢日元與能源漲價，待能源回穩、日元過度疲軟獲矯正，通膨可望放緩，使日本經濟與日元進入「良性循環」。此番表態被市場解讀為華府公開押注日本央行 (BOJ) 在 9 月 17-18 日會議上升息。
貝森特長期呼籲日本升息，此次更把匯率干預與貨幣政策掛鉤。他強調，美日上週五 (7 月 31 日) 罕見聯手買入日元，為 1998 年來首度聯合買日元、2011 年後再度協調干預，意在防止弱勢日元引爆亞洲貨幣競貶、動盪蔓延。
貝森特說，「干預釋放信號，但真正改變走勢的是政策」，並稱美方透過紐約聯準銀行賣歐元買日元，此舉兼具「象徵日美合作信任」之意，也避免日本國債失錨連動推高美國長債殖利率。
他還表示，8 月底 G20 財金首長會議將與植田會面，並示警稱日本國債作為全球利率基準的角色不能動搖，美日對「日債安全健全」認知一致。
分析師指出，美國親自下場不全然為日本著想，更憂心日元套利交易反轉與日債拋售潮蔓延至美債市場。短期匯率紅線已由聯合干預劃出，但利差問題未解，BOJ 下月是否升息仍看日本薪資與核心通膨數據。
paras_en: US Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen expressed her confidence in Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Kazuo Ueda's ability to make the best decisions for Japan's economy in an interview with NHK on Tuesday. Yellen, who has known Ueda for over 15 years, stated that she believes Ueda will adopt the most beneficial economic policies for Japan. She also noted that Japan's inflation is partly driven by a weak yen and rising energy prices, and that once energy prices stabilize and the yen's excessive weakness is corrected, inflation is expected to ease, leading Japan's economy and currency into a 'virtuous cycle'. This statement has been interpreted by the market as a sign that the US is openly betting on the BOJ to raise interest rates at its meeting on September 17-18.

Yellen has long been advocating for Japan to raise interest rates, and this time she linked currency intervention to monetary policy. She emphasized that the US and Japan's rare joint purchase of yen last Friday (July 31) was the first time they had done so since 1998, and the second time they had coordinated intervention since 2011, aiming to prevent a weak yen from triggering an Asian currency depreciation and spreading turmoil.

Yellen stated that 'intervention sends a signal, but it's policy that truly changes the trend', and noted that the US sold euros to buy yen through the New York Federal Reserve, which not only symbolized the trust between the US and Japan but also prevented Japan's bond yields from rising and affecting US long-term interest rates.

She also mentioned that she will meet with Ueda at the G20 finance ministers' meeting at the end of August and warned that Japan's role as a global interest rate benchmark cannot be shaken, with the US and Japan sharing the same understanding of the importance of 'Japan's bond safety and soundness'.

Analysts pointed out that the US's personal involvement is not entirely for Japan's benefit, but rather due to concerns about the potential reversal of yen arbitrage trades and the spread of Japanese bond sell-offs to the US bond market. While the short-term exchange rate red line has been drawn by the joint intervention, the issue of interest rate differentials remains unresolved, and whether the BOJ will raise interest rates next month still depends on Japan's wage and core inflation data.

items.title: 賣歐元買日元 美國財長：不惜一切代價支持日本
items.title_en: Sell Euros, Buy Yen: U.S. Treasury Secretary Says He Will Support Japan at Any Cost
paras: 美國財政部長貝森特周二（4 日）表示，在有利於美國經濟的前提下，川普政府將「不惜一切代價」支持日本穩定匯市。
他在接受《CNBC》節目採訪時稱：「我們將竭盡全力支持日本，前提是對美國經濟和美國納稅人有益。」
貝森特在節目中說，美國已加入日本提振日元的聯合干預行動，原因是日元持續疲軟可能破壞整個亞洲市場穩定，甚至引發其他貨幣競爭性貶值，「這種情況很不健康」。
他強調：「考慮到貿易流量、經濟規模以及日本對全球儲蓄市場的貢獻，保持日元穩定至關重要。日本政府明白這一點，我國很榮幸與日本合作，共同落實相關政策，協助地區穩定。」
《CNBC》指出，此次美日聯合干預是美國支持另一主要貨幣的罕見舉措，凸顯出華府對日元長期疲軟可能加劇日本通膨、打壓其他亞洲貨幣、擾亂全球市場的擔憂。
作為美日聯合行動的一部分，美國財政部出售了外匯儲備中的歐元，並將所得資金用於買入日元。貝森特說，他已向歐洲官員說明出售歐元僅為儲備資產重新配置。
「在我看來，歐元匯率已更接近均衡水準，」貝森特說，「我不會評論歐元應該在什麼位置交易，但真正的問題在於日元目前被嚴重低估，以及日本政府正在採取哪些應對措施。」
不過，貝森特也強調，購入日元只能在短期內抑制市場波動，日本仍需通過根本性政策調整應對日元走弱的深層因素。
paras_en: U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen said on Tuesday (the 4th) that, provided it benefits the U.S. economy, the Trump administration will "support Japan at any cost" to stabilize the foreign‑exchange market.
In an interview with CNBC, she said, "We will do everything we can to support Japan, as long as it is beneficial to the U.S. economy and American taxpayers."

Yellen explained that the United States has joined Japan’s coordinated intervention to boost the yen because a persistently weak yen could undermine stability across Asian markets and even trigger competitive devaluations of other currencies, which she called "very unhealthy."

She emphasized, "Given trade flows, economic size, and Japan’s contribution to the global savings market, keeping the yen stable is crucial. The Japanese government understands this, and we are honored to work with Japan to implement the relevant policies and help regional stability."

CNBC noted that this U.S.–Japan joint intervention is a rare instance of Washington backing another major currency, highlighting concerns that a prolonged weak yen could exacerbate Japanese inflation, depress other Asian currencies, and disrupt global markets.

As part of the joint action, the U.S. Treasury sold euros from its foreign‑exchange reserves and used the proceeds to buy yen. Yellen said she has told European officials that the euro sale is simply a reallocation of reserve assets.

"In my view, the euro exchange rate is now closer to a balanced level," Yellen said. "I won’t comment on where the euro should be trading, but the real issue is that the yen is severely undervalued right now, and what measures the Japanese government is taking in response."

However, Yellen also stressed that buying yen can only dampen market volatility in the short term; Japan still needs fundamental policy adjustments to address the deeper drivers of the yen’s weakness.

美國 7 月製造業採購經理人指數 (PMI) 升至逾四年新高，並據美國總統川普表示與伊朗的談判正在進行，警告德黑蘭這是簽署一項良好協議的最後機會，但伊朗否認與美國進行或計畫進行任何談判，促使投資人權衡美國和伊朗潛在談判的矛盾信號，並等待一系列美國勞動力市場報告，以尋找美國聯邦準備理事會 (FED) 利率走向的線索；此外，週二日本經濟財政大臣城內實稱，迄今為止日本消費者物價僅溫和上漲，中東衝突導致成本上升對物價的傳導作用仍有限，對通貨膨脹風險表達相對樂觀態度，但曾經參與東京十多年前外匯市場干預行動的前日本央行 (BOJ) 官員竹內淳表示，若日圓重新出現走弱跡象，日本和美國肯定會再次採取聯合干預行動，並據 BOJ 發布研究報告指出，日本基礎通貨膨脹加速等經濟基本面的變化，可能是近期長期利率上升的背後原因，隨著 BOJ 持續縮減公債購買規模，日本公債市場的功能明顯改善，而且市場警惕後續干預，令美元兌日圓盤整於 157.15 低點。

據美國財政部長貝森特稱，將不惜一切代價支持日本穩定匯率的努力，而且 BOJ 數據顯示，日本在最新一輪旨在提振日圓匯率的干預行動中，可能已斥資高達 365.8 億美元，但週二數據並未顯示 BOJ 經常帳戶餘額出現大規模資金外流，通常大規模資金外流被認為與干預規模存在關聯，並據美國商務部 6 月數據顯示，工廠訂單意外下降 0.3%，但耐久財訂單修正後增幅擴大至 0.5% 及貿易逆差收窄 5.6% 降至 733 億美元，而且美國勞工統計局發布的職位空缺與勞動力流動調查 (JOLTS) 顯示，截至 6 月底衡量勞動力需求職位空缺減少 17.8 萬個，但招聘人數增加且裁員人數保持低位，意味著勞動力市場依然穩定，提振美元兌日圓至 157.95 高點。預估今日美元兌日圓阻力於 157.70-90，支撐於 156.70-90。
◆EUR/USD
昨日澳洲 6 月數據顯示，儘管借貸成本上升，但駕駛者購買新電動汽車應對高油價，家庭支出穩健增長 0.8%，同時招聘廣告數量增加 0.8%，表明勞動力和需求仍堅挺，為必要時再加息提供空間，並據紐西蘭央行 (RBNZ) 暗示可能進一步升息，支撐澳幣和紐元，而且美元多倉規模創紀錄，引發行情急轉風險升溫，扶助歐元兌美元穩守 1.1501 低點。
隨後卡塔爾表示，調解方在結束美國和伊朗衝突的努力中取得進展，美國財政部長貝森特亦稱，可能週二或週三達成恢復荷姆茲海峽通航協議，激發樂觀情緒，推升歐元兌美元至 1.1534 高點。預估今日歐元兌美元阻力於 1.1540-60，支撐於 1.1460-80。
◆GBP/USD
週二市場等待美國和伊朗和平談判的消息，同時警惕日本與美國實施進一步干預，導致英鎊兌美元徘徊於 1.3415 低點。隨著市場關注週五美國就業報告，以調整對 FED 加息的預期，但美國國務卿魯比奧稱，荷姆茲海峽通航相關磋商已取得進展，激勵英鎊兌美元回升至 1.3455 高點。預估今日英鎊兌美元阻力於 1.3450-70，支撐於 1.3370-90。

items.title: 〈紐約匯市〉美元持平 日元走弱但仍遠高於干預前低點
items.title_en: Dollar Holds Steady as Yen Weakens but Remains Above 40-Year Low
paras: 美元周二 (4 日) 變動不大，外匯市場焦點仍集中在日元走勢。雖然日元兌美元回落，但仍明顯高於上周美日聯手干預匯市前所觸及的 40 年低點。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數 (DXY) 幾乎持平，報 99.88。
美國財政部長貝森特 (Scott Bessent) 本周稍早證實，美國已與日本聯手進場買進日元，這是 2011 年以來雙方首次聯合干預匯市，也是美國自 1998 年以來首度直接出手支持日元匯價。
貝森特周二接受 CNBC 採訪時表示，美方之所以協助日本，是因為日元持續貶值可能對亞洲金融市場帶來不穩定影響。
他表示，「考量到貿易流量、日本經濟規模及其對全球儲蓄市場的重要性，維持日元穩定非常重要。日本政府了解這點，我們也很榮幸能與日本攜手推動相關政策，協助穩定區域市場。」
在此次干預前，日元兌美元一度跌至 164 日元，創下 40 年新低。日元走弱將對高度依賴進口的日本經濟帶來壓力。日本也是全球持有美國公債最多的海外國家，因此日元匯率波動一直受到市場高度關注。
AJ Bell 投資總監 Russ Mould 表示，「這十年來日元貶值幅度之大，以至於華府與東京都不得不聯手支撐匯價。不過，美國的參與恐怕並非完全無私。相較於日本首相高市早苗 (Sanae Takaichi) 所面臨的債務與通膨問題，美國財長貝森特更擔心的是，日本若出售龐大的美國公債部位，可能對市場造成衝擊。」
華爾街策略師指出，美國明確表示願意動用資源協助干預，意味著市場過去認為單一央行受限於外匯存底的「儲備上限」限制已大幅降低。
為降低市場干預可能對金融市場造成的衝擊，美日兩國財政部也表示，未來將利用聯準會的外國與國際貨幣當局附買回機制 (Foreign and International Monetary Authorities, FIMA Repo Facility)，在後續市場操作中提供流動性支持。
Brown Brothers Harriman 市場策略主管 Elias Haddad 表示，「任何反彈都可能只是短暫的，並成為逢高賣出美元兌日元的機會。美日聯手干預，加上官員明確表示必要時將再次出手，大幅提高市場與官方對作的成本，也使美元兌日元的上行空間受到更明顯限制。」
美元兌日元上漲 0.4%，至 157.76。
美元持平 市場聚焦就業數據
在上周受到聯準會利率前景不明，以及美日聯手干預日元等因素影響而大幅下跌後，美元指數本周大致維持區間整理。
市場本周將持續關注美國勞動市場數據，以尋找聯準會 (Fed) 未來利率政策方向的新線索。
美國勞工統計局周二公布，6 月 JOLTS 職缺數為 735.9 萬個，低於市場預估的 745.4 萬個。5 月職缺數也由原先公布的 759.4 萬個下修至 753.7 萬個，而 4 月職缺數曾升至 758.5 萬個，創下 2024 年 5 月以來新高。
雖然 6 月職缺數低於市場預期，但整體報告仍顯示，美國就業市場依舊保持穩健。
這份數據也支持聯準會近期將政策重心重新放在抑制通膨。由於充分就業目標目前已大致達成，因此聯準會目前更專注於通膨任務。
另一方面，中東衝突導致油價波動，也改變了市場對通膨的預期，並使聯準會官員對未來貨幣政策方向出現分歧。
這周勞動市場數據的重頭戲，將是周五公布的 7 月非農就業報告。
其他主要貨幣方面，歐元兌美元上漲 0.2%，至 1 歐元兌 1.1531 美元。
英鎊兌美元也上漲 0.2%，至 1 英鎊兌 1.3450 美元。
中東局勢持續受到關注。國際油價周二連續第二個交易日下跌，有助於抑制通膨壓力。
貝森特接受 CNBC 訪問時表示，他相信美國與伊朗正接近達成協議，「我們有機會在今天或明天達成協議，重新開放荷姆茲海峽 (Strait of Hormuz)，讓這場衝突逐步回到較為正常的狀態。」
此外，卡達表示，促成伊朗衝突外交解決方案的努力仍在持續，目前談判重點包括局勢降溫，以及重新開放荷姆茲海峽。
根據媒體報導，作為美國與伊朗之間的重要區域調解者，卡達透露，協議草案文字已經完成，並正在各談判方之間傳閱。
雖然目前各方尚未同意展開直接談判，但卡達表示，短期內達成一項初步協議仍是目前最主要目標。

paras_en: The dollar was relatively unchanged on Tuesday, with the foreign exchange market's focus still on the yen's trajectory. Although the yen fell against the dollar, it remained significantly higher than the 40-year low it touched before the US-Japan intervention last week.
At the New York close, the dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six major currencies, was almost unchanged at 99.88.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed earlier this week that the US had intervened in the foreign exchange market with Japan, a move that marked the first joint intervention since 2011 and the first direct US support for the yen since 1998.
Bessent told CNBC on Tuesday that the US was helping Japan because a continued decline in the yen could have destabilizing effects on Asian financial markets.

He said, "Given the importance of trade flows, Japan's economic size, and its importance to global savings markets, maintaining a stable yen is crucial. The Japanese government understands this, and we're honored to be working with them to implement policies that help stabilize the region's markets."

Before the intervention, the yen had fallen to 164 yen per dollar, a 40-year low. A weaker yen would put pressure on Japan's economy, which relies heavily on imports. Japan is also the largest foreign holder of US debt, making the yen's exchange rate highly watched by the market.

Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell, said, "The scale of the yen's decline over the past decade has been so great that Washington and Tokyo have had to join forces to support the currency. However, the US involvement may not be entirely altruistic. Compared to Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's debt and inflation problems, US Treasury Secretary Bessent is more concerned about the potential impact of Japan selling its large US Treasury holdings on the market."

Wall Street strategists noted that the US has made it clear that it is willing to use its resources to intervene, implying that the market's previous assumption that a single central bank was limited by its foreign exchange reserves "reserve constraint" has been significantly reduced.

To minimize the impact of the intervention on financial markets, the US and Japanese finance ministries said they would use the Federal Reserve's Foreign and International Monetary Authorities (FIMA) Repo Facility to provide liquidity support in future market operations.

Elias Haddad, market strategy head at Brown Brothers Harriman, said, "Any rebound could be short-lived and become an opportunity to sell the dollar-yen pair. The joint US-Japan intervention, combined with officials' statements that they would intervene again if necessary, has significantly increased the cost of trading and has limited the dollar-yen pair's upside space."
The dollar-yen pair rose 0.4% to 157.76.
The dollar held steady as the market focused on US employment data.

After a sharp decline last week due to uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's interest rate outlook and the US-Japan intervention in the yen, the dollar index has maintained a trading range this week.
The market will continue to focus on US labor market data to find new clues about the Federal Reserve's future interest rate policy direction.
The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Tuesday that the June JOLTS job openings number was 7.359 million, lower than the market's estimate of 7.454 million.
The May job openings number was also revised downward to 7.537 million from the previously reported 7.594 million, while the April job openings number had risen to 7.585 million, a new high for 2024.
Although the June job openings number was lower than expected, the overall report showed that the US labor market remains stable.
This data also supports the Federal Reserve's recent shift in policy focus to inflation suppression, as the full employment target has been largely achieved.
On the other hand, the Middle East conflict has changed market expectations for inflation, and Federal Reserve officials have differing views on future monetary policy direction.
The highlight of this week's labor market data will be the release of the July non-farm employment report on Friday.
Other major currencies, the euro rose 0.2% against the dollar to 1.1531 euros per dollar, and the pound rose 0.2% against the dollar to 1.3450 pounds per dollar.
The Middle East situation remains a concern, with international oil prices falling for the second consecutive trading day, helping to ease inflationary pressures.

Bessent told CNBC that he believes the US and Iran are close to reaching an agreement, "We have a chance to reach an agreement today or tomorrow, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and bring this conflict back to a more normal state."
Qatar also said that efforts to promote a diplomatic solution to the Iran conflict are ongoing, with a focus on de-escalating tensions and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
According to media reports, as a key mediator in the US-Iran conflict, Qatar revealed that the draft agreement text has been completed and is being circulated among the negotiating parties.
Although the parties have not yet agreed to hold direct talks, Qatar said that reaching a preliminary agreement in the short term remains the main goal.

items.title: 美國為何突然出手救日元？貝森特最怕亞洲貨幣競貶
items.title_en: Why Is the United States Suddenly Acting to Save the Yen? Bessent’s Biggest Fear Is an Asian Currency Devaluation Race
paras: 美國財政部長貝森特 (Scott Bessent) 周二 (4 日) 表示，美國之所以罕見加入日本的買進日元行動，是因為日元持續疲弱可能迫使其他亞洲國家競相讓本幣貶值，進而動搖區域及全球金融市場。
貝森特接受《CNBC》節目「Squawk Box」訪問時表示，穩定的日元不僅對美國重要，對整個亞洲也相當關鍵。他指出，日元若大幅貶值，可能對其他國家形成貨幣貶值壓力，目前韓元已出現劇烈波動，人民幣匯率也存在遭到低估的疑慮。
貝森特表示，考量日本的貿易規模、經濟體量，以及日本對全球儲蓄市場的貢獻，維持日元穩定至關重要。日本政府了解這一點，美方也樂於支持日本落實相關政策，共同協助穩定亞洲市場。
此次行動是美國罕見出手支撐另一種主要貨幣，凸顯華府擔心日元長期疲弱不僅會推高日本進口成本與通膨，也可能壓迫其他亞洲貨幣，甚至將金融動盪擴散至全球市場。
在這次美日聯合干預中，美國財政部動用外匯存底出售歐元，再將所得資金用於買進日元。貝森特表示，他已向歐洲官員保證，出售歐元只是美國外匯存底的重新配置，並非刻意打壓歐元。
貝森特指出，美日是在日元遭到「嚴重低估」後，聯手進場買進日元。兩國政府此前一直保持密切聯繫，華府也相信日本將採取適當政策，使日元逐步回到較為正常的水準。
不過，貝森特坦言，干預只能在短期內抑制匯市波動，無法單獨決定日元的長期走勢。他強調，政府可以透過干預向市場發出訊號，但真正扭轉匯率方向的仍是政策。
貝森特拒絕直接評論日本央行是否應該升息，僅表示日本官員必須在干預後推出更廣泛的政策，處理造成日元走弱的根本因素。美國決定參與此次行動，正是因為對日本接下來的政策路線抱持樂觀態度。
paras_en: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday (the 4th) that the United States’ rare decision to join Japan in buying yen is driven by the concern that a persistently weak yen could force other Asian countries to competitively devalue their own currencies, thereby destabilising regional and global financial markets.

In an interview on CNBC’s “Squawk Box,” Bessent stressed that a stable yen is not only important for the United States but also crucial for the entire Asian region. He warned that a sharp depreciation of the yen could create downward pressure on other currencies – the Korean won is already showing extreme volatility, and there are doubts that the renminbi is being undervalued.

Bessent noted that, given Japan’s trade size, economic weight and its contribution to the global savings market, keeping the yen stable is essential. The Japanese government understands this, and the U.S. is happy to support Japan in implementing related policies to help stabilise Asian markets jointly.

This intervention marks a rare instance of the United States backing another major currency, highlighting Washington’s worry that prolonged yen weakness would not only raise Japan’s import costs and inflation but also pressure other Asian currencies and potentially spread financial turbulence worldwide.

In the joint U.S.-Japan intervention, the Treasury used foreign‑exchange reserves to sell euros and then used the proceeds to buy yen. Bessent said he has assured European officials that the euro sales are merely a reallocation of U.S. reserves, not an intentional move to suppress the euro.

Bessent explained that the U.S. and Japan entered the market after the yen was deemed “severely undervalued.” The two governments have been in close contact, and Washington believes Japan will adopt appropriate policies to gradually bring the yen back to a more normal level.

However, Bessent admitted that intervention can only curb short‑term FX volatility and cannot determine the yen’s long‑term trajectory on its own. He emphasized that while governments can signal intentions through intervention, the real driver of exchange‑rate direction remains policy.

Bessent declined to comment directly on whether the Bank of Japan should raise rates, saying only that Japanese officials need to follow the intervention with broader measures that address the underlying factors behind the yen’s weakness. The United States chose to participate because it is optimistic about Japan’s forthcoming policy path.

items.title_en: Exporters and Central Bank Bailout Narrow TWD Depreciation, Guarding the 32.5‑Per‑Dollar Barrier
paras: 台股今 (4) 日走勢震盪小跌作收，新台幣兌美元盤中再度面臨 32.5 元關卡保衛戰，但央行持續介入穩匯，加上出口商擴大拋匯，帶動匯價拉升至平盤附近，以 32.447 元作收，微貶 0.9 分，為連 2 貶，台北與元太外匯市場總成交值萎縮至 24.7 億美元。
新台幣兌美元今天開盤報 32.447 元，午後在外資擴大匯出下，匯價一度下探至 32.495 元，距 32.5 元大關僅一步之遙。隨著匯價來到相對低點，出口商隨即進場擴大拋匯，台幣貶幅縮小；加上央行尾盤適時調節，終場幾乎回吐午後所有貶幅，收在 32.447 元。

paras_en: Taiwan’s stock market edged lower in a volatile session today, while the New Taiwan dollar (NTD) faced another test at the 32.5 per USD level. The central bank’s continued intervention helped stabilize the exchange rate, and exporters’ increased foreign‑currency sales pushed the rate back toward the flat‑rate area, closing at 32.447 NTD per USD, a modest 0.9‑point decline and the second consecutive drop. The total turnover in Taipei and Yuan‑Tai foreign‑exchange markets shrank to US$2.47 billion.

The NTD opened at 32.447 per USD. In the afternoon, foreign investors expanded their currency outflows, briefly driving the rate to 32.495, just a hair away from the 32.5 threshold. As the rate hit this relative low, exporters stepped in with larger currency sales, narrowing the depreciation. Coupled with timely adjustments by the central bank near the close, the market almost fully recovered the afternoon’s losses, ending again at 32.447.

Looking at major currencies against the dollar, central‑bank data show the US Dollar Index rose 0.19%. The Japanese yen, after yesterday’s surge, fell 0.65% today. The Korean won slipped 0.33%, the Singapore dollar 0.12%, the New Taiwan dollar a modest 0.03% decline, while the Chinese yuan edged up 0.03%, indicating a general weakening of Asian currencies.

U.S. equities rallied strongly yesterday, but Taiwan’s market fell nearly 500 points after the open, led down by TSMC. Electronics heavyweights showed mixed moves, while sectors such as silicon photonics, printed circuit boards and memory chips attracted buying. The overall market’s decline narrowed, closing at 43,360.66 points, down 25.75 points.
